class.name: NetwSceneHandle
class.brief_description: The scene an entity belongs to, reached as [member NetwEntity.scene].
class.description: The view a game holds for one scene: who is in it, who may enter it, and when that changes. It holds no authoritative state, so it can be reconstructed at any moment. One scene has one handle, so [code]==[/code] returns "the same scene" and a listener connected through any route hears every edge. Reach it with [method Netw.scene] or [member NetwEntity.scene]. Never [code]null[/code] for an entity in a session: an entity that declares itself a scene resolves to itself, and any other entity resolves to its nearest scene ancestor. Ask [member is_declared] when the difference matters. [codeblock] func _on_scene_live(track: NetwSceneHandle) -> void: track.player_entered.connect(_on_car_entered) track.player_left.connect(_on_car_left) for participant in track.participants: track.admit(participant) [/codeblock] A view resolves its session through the branch its scene node sits in, so a scene whose container is not in the tree returns [member is_declared] [code]false[/code] and every other member empty. [NetwMultiplayer] keeps the same surface keyed by [RID] for callers that already hold one, and [member entity] is the bridge to it: [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_get_players], [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_admit] and [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_observe] are the flat spellings of [member players], [method admit] and the signals here.

method.name: add_player
method.description: Seats [param player] in this scene through [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_add_player], which admits the player and parents its node under [member root]. The one call that seats a freshly instantiated player: parenting alone makes it a member, because membership is ancestry, but its peer still has to be admitted before the subtree is replicated to it. Admission is flushed before the node enters the tree, so the spawn packets the subtree produces already target the peer about to receive them. Only authority admits; every peer still parents its own copy. [codeblock] var node := template.instantiate_player(participant) NetwEntity.of(self).scene.add_player(NetwEntity.of(node)) [/codeblock] [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK parented, and admitted when this peer is authority ┠╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER peer_id 0, while admitting ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST this scene names no live node ┖╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE no player, no session, or admission failed [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: admit
method.description: Admits [param participant] to this scene, which is what makes the scene's subtree replicate to that peer and what seats the participant here. Idempotent, so admitting a participant this scene already admits changes nothing. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK admitted ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED this peer is not the server ┠╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER a null participant, outside a session, or a peer id of 0 ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST this scene names no live node ┖╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE admission did not take, after everything else succeeded [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: admits
method.description: Whether this scene currently admits [param participant]. Reads the admission boundary rather than the seat, so it returns for a participant admitted before it was seated.

method.name: move
method.description: Moves [param entity] into THIS scene, returning the [NetwPromise] the settle carries. [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_move] holds the law, the carry window included; what differs here is the direction the call reads in, because the destination is the object the verb is called on and the mover is what it takes. [codeblock] var moved := destination.move(NetwEntity.of(player), opts) await moved.wait() [/codeblock] Returns an already-settled [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] for a null [param entity] or outside a session. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: observe
method.description:
Calls [param callback] whenever this scene gains or loses a subject of [param event], one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.SceneEvent]. Registering the same [param callback] for the same [param event] twice does nothing. [b]The callback is handed the subject as the object a game holds, never as the internal handle the scene book keys its rows by.[/b] That is the one place this class does more than forward: [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_observe] hands a raw subject straight through, and a game writing this signature would have to name an [RID] it can do nothing with. [codeblock] arena.observe(NetwMultiplayer.SCENE_EVENT_PLAYER, on_car_edge)
func on_car_edge(present: bool, car: NetwEntity) -> bool: reshuffle(car) return false # true drops the subscription [/codeblock] [constant NetwMultiplayer.SCENE_EVENT_PARTICIPANT] carries a [NetwParticipant]; [constant NetwMultiplayer.SCENE_EVENT_PLAYER] and [constant NetwMultiplayer.SCENE_EVENT_ENTITY] carry a [NetwEntity]. Returning [code]true[/code] from the callback withdraws it, exactly as the flat verb's does, and [method unobserve] withdraws it by name.

method.name: release
method.description: Withdraws [param participant]'s admission, so the scene's subtree stops replicating to that peer. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the admission is withdrawn ┠╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER this handle has no session, or a null participant ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST the scene did not admit them [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: unobserve
method.description: Withdraws the [param callback] a [method observe] call registered for [param event]. It must be the same [Callable] that was passed to [method observe], because that is the name the relay is filed under; a fresh [Callable] over the same method is a different name and withdraws nothing.

members.member: Every entity standing in this scene, as the [NetwEntity] each one is read through. [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_get_entities] returns the same set under the flat spelling, as the internal handles the session keys its rows by; this member resolves each one so a caller never holds an [RID] it would only hand straight back.

The resolved scene's entity RID, or an invalid RID outside a session. Resolution is self-inclusive and walks the parent-entity chain, so it follows the tree and self-heals on reparent without anything re-enrolling the entity. This is the identity every [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_find]-family verb works on, and the bridge from the entity sugar to the flat surface.

Whether a scene resolved at all. [code]false[/code] for an entity outside every scene, where every other member reads empty. The session-keyed read for a resolved scene is [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_is_declared] over [member entity].
The name this scene was declared under, which is the name [method Netw.scene] and [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_find] resolve.
The player entity this peer represents in this scene, or [code]null[/code] when this peer has none here.
Every participant seated in this scene. A participant is a person in the session; a player is the entity they steer, and [member players] returns those.
Every player entity in this scene, in no declared order.

The authored node this scene was declared on, which is the scene's own identity, or [code]null[/code] outside a session. This is the node a game parents content under and reparents players into. [method Netw.spawn] returns [member world] rather than this node when the scene declared [method NetwSceneConfig.isolated], so a caller that spawned an isolated scene reads the root back through here.

The [SubViewport] the framework inserted above [member root] to give this scene a [World2D] and [World3D] of its own, or [code]null[/code] for a scene that shares the session's world. Only a [Viewport] owns a world in Godot, so [method NetwSceneConfig.isolated] is delivered by inserting one rather than by a flag on the authored root. It carries no scene identity of its own and every materializing peer inserts the same one.

signal.name: participant_entered
signal.description: Emitted when [param participant] is seated in this scene, after the admission boundary is written, so a listener reading [member participants] sees them.

signal.name: participant_left
signal.description: Emitted when [param participant] leaves this scene, whether by moving to another or by leaving the session.

signal.name: player_entered
signal.description: Emitted when [param player] joins this scene's roster. A join changes what every other player in the scene is compared against, so a listener that maintains per-player state rebuilds the whole roster here rather than only the newcomer.

signal.name: player_left
signal.description: Emitted when [param player] leaves this scene's roster.
